guide.subtitle: Everything you need to use SoundScout in the classroom
guide.moreVideosDescription: The general tutorial section of SoundScout has extra videos about the studio, effects, saving and sharing — handy to show your students too.

getting-started.title: Getting started
content: Welcome! SoundScout is a web app where students learn to compose music by collecting sounds at locations and placing them on a timeline. As a teacher you have your own dashboard to manage classes, set up assignments, and review submissions.
You need a teacher account. Register via the login page — click 'No account yet?' and follow the steps. You'll receive a confirmation email; activate your account via the link.

After logging in, create your first class using the 'New class' button. Each class automatically gets a 4-digit class code. Share that code with your students — they enter it on the start screen to be linked to your class.
Tip: write the class code on the whiteboard or print it on a worksheet. Students can also enter via a link with the class code embedded (handy when using a Chromebook cart).

classes.title: Managing classes
content: Your dashboard shows all classes you've created. You can have up to 8 classes simultaneously (free account). Each class has its own class code that doesn't change — students only need it once.
To delete a class, use the trash icon on the class card. Note: deleting a class also removes all related submissions, templates, and praatplaten. This cannot be undone.
Click a class to open the detail view. There you see all student submissions, can activate assignments (template or praatplaat), and see compositions still 'In progress'.

assignments.title: Setting up assignments
content: SoundScout has two types of assignments: templates and praatplaten (sound maps). Templates are pre-structured compositions students build on — ideal for focused exercises. Praatplaten are collaborative activities where students place their composition on a location on an image, which you as teacher can present afterwards.

Each class can have one active assignment at a time. Students entering the class code are automatically routed: with a template they start in the studio using your composition as a starting point; with a praatplaat they first choose a position on the image.
Set up assignments in the class detail screen. It has tabs for templates and praatplaten, with buttons to create new ones or activate existing ones.

compose-modes.title: Composition modes
content: When a student clicks 'New Composition', they first choose a mode. Each mode suits a different learning objective.

The student picks a theme (e.g. The City or Winter Games) and explores freely. There are no images or sections — the student decides the structure. This suits open-ended assignments and independent exploration.

The student picks an image (e.g. King's Day, Sports Field) and creates a soundscape to match that scene. The theme is automatically determined by the image. This suits listening and sound-illustration tasks: 'What sounds do you hear in this place?'

The student picks a story of multiple images (e.g. Start → Jump → Landing). The timeline is automatically divided into sections matching the images, so the student practises musical structure and form. This suits assignments about tension, contrast and structure.

As a teacher you can also link a template to a storyboard. The student then gets a fixed composition as starting point, including the storyboard's sections and images. This combines a guided assignment with visual support.

templates.title: Creating templates
content: A template is a composition you prepare as a starting point for students. For example: an empty track structure, a fixed rhythm, or a half-finished song that students complete.

Build a composition in the studio, then choose 'Save as template' (in the Stage screen, under 'Share & Export'). You can give it a name and description, and choose lock options: can students modify existing clips? Can they add tracks? Is the sample library locked?

After saving, the template appears in your dashboard. Activate it for a specific class via the class detail screen. Note: a template is linked to a theme — students automatically get the same theme you used.

praatplaat.title: Using a praatplaat
content: A praatplaat is a collaborative sound map: each student creates a small composition and places it on a position on an image (e.g. a forest, a city, a market). As teacher you can then present the praatplaat to the class — click a spot and hear what that student made.

Go to the class detail screen and click 'Activate an assignment'. Choose 'Praatplaat', enter a name (e.g. 'Sounds at the market — grade 5a') and choose a location image from the active theme. Each class can only have one active assignment at a time.

Students enter the 4-digit class code on the start screen. They then see a preview of the praatplaat. After clicking 'Start' they choose a spot on the image where they want to place their composition. Then they build their composition as usual in the studio. When they save, the composition is automatically linked to the chosen spot. Using the 'Choose a new spot' button they can then add another composition at a different location.

Open the praatplaat via 'Open praatplaat' next to the active assignment. You see the image fullscreen with speaker icons at the spots where students placed compositions. Click an icon to play the composition. If multiple students are close together, spots are automatically clustered — you then pick from a list. Click the refresh icon in the top right to load newly added compositions.

Click 'Share link' next to the active praatplaat. You get a direct URL and a QR code. Students who open this link or scan the QR code go directly into the praatplaat flow without needing to enter the class code manually. Ideal for projecting on the whiteboard.

At the bottom of the share dialog you'll find the 'Listening page' option. Click 'Create listening page' to generate a public link. Anyone with this link — including parents, colleagues or guests — can view the praatplaat and listen to all compositions, without logging in. The link is valid for 30 days and can be extended by clicking the button again. A QR code is also available for printing or sharing.

submissions.title: Reviewing submissions
content: The class detail screen shows all compositions students have shared with your class. Each submission shows the student's name, date, and a play button.
'Submitted' shows formally submitted compositions. 'In progress' shows compositions students have saved locally but not yet submitted (marked with a badge and 'Last edited' timestamp).
Per submission you can listen, view details (timeline view), and export to MP3. This way you can review student work, provide feedback, or use compositions in a class presentation.

save-codes.title: Save codes for students
content: Students often work on shared devices. Save codes let them continue on another device — for example, finish at home what they started at school.

Three code types students may encounter: a 4-digit class code (to link to your class), a 6-character save code (to save their own composition and continue later), and an 8-character share or template code (for listen-only or opening a template).

A student creates a save code in the studio or stage screen via 'Save online'. The app shows a 6-character code and a QR code; the student writes it down or scans it on the other device. On that device they enter the code on the start screen to continue.
Compositions with a save code automatically expire after 60 days of inactivity. If a student continues working, the counter resets.

classroom-tips.title: Classroom tips
content: Headphones are almost essential. Without them it's chaotic in a class of 25 students playing sounds at once. Tip: set Chromebook volumes to max 50% class-wide to prevent hearing damage.

Browsers block audio by default until the user clicks. SoundScout handles this on the first click or tap — students don't need to do anything, but if there's no sound, have them tap the screen. If a sample really won't load, refresh the page — the composition is saved locally.

SoundScout works on Chromebooks and iPads. iPad: use landscape orientation for more workspace. Safari works best. Chromebook: make sure the device doesn't go to sleep during recordings — it interrupts the web audio system.
Plan about 15-20 minutes for first exploration (exploring, collecting sounds), and 30-45 minutes for actual composing. A complete lesson with template or praatplaat usually fits in a 45-minute block.

privacy.title: Privacy & data
privacy.dataText: Compositions you create are stored on your own device (in the browser). No account is created and no personal data is collected. If you save a composition online with a save code, it is temporarily stored in the cloud and automatically deleted after 60 days of inactivity.
privacy.classCodeText: When you use a class code, your composition is shared with the teacher of that class. The teacher can listen to and view your composition via the teacher dashboard. Your name is only visible if you entered it yourself.
privacy.cookiesText: SoundScout does not use tracking cookies, analytics or advertisements. The only local storage is for your compositions and language preference. No data is shared with third parties.
privacy.contact: Questions about privacy? Contact us at <mail>bvanuffelen@gmail.com</mail>.
